Bug_Title: "Object.wait()", "Object.notify()" and "Object.notifyAll()" should only be called from synchronized code
Bug_Details:
The Object.wait(…​) , Object.notify() and Object.notifyAll() methods are used in multithreaded environments
to coordinate interdependent tasks that are performed by different threads. These methods are not thread-safe and by contract, they require the
invoking Thread to own the object’s monitor. If a thread invokes one of these methods without owning the object’s monitor an IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is in the showBug method. The wait() and notify()/notifyAll() methods are being called outside of a synchronized block, which is not allowed as per the Java Language Specification

Model_Explanation: The provided Java code does not contain the described bug. The Object.wait(), Object.notify() and Object.notifyAll() methods are called from synchronized code blocks. The synchronized keyword ensures that only one thread can execute the synchronized code block at a time, thus preventing race conditions. The wait() method releases the lock and the thread goes into waiting state, and the notify() or notifyAll() method wakes up the waiting thread.
